text: Harness: executor backends - built-in tool loop, or delegate coding leaves to Claude Code / Codex in a worktree
description: Executor interface: execute(idea, compiledContext, worktree, budget) -> {diff, commands run, claimed evidence, usage}. Backend 1: the existing AI SDK tool loop (read/search/str_replace/run_command). Backend 2: headless CLI agents (claude -p / codex exec --json) in a disposable git worktree; reuse the Codex adapter with authoritative telemetry from 02e512d5. The harness, not the CLI agent, writes results to the graph. Lets strong coding agents do the code while the harness keeps the loop, context and verification.

status.comment: Done: harness.json executor.backend = builtin (AI SDK tool loop, default) | claude-code. packages/loop-worker/src/claude-code-executor.ts runs `claude -p` in the loop's execution path with the compiled context as prompt, --json-schema = the execution result schema (structured_output becomes the stage result), --strict-mcp-config (no graph tools: the harness alone writes the graph), --setting-sources user + AIMPARENCY_ALLOW_STOP=1 (the repo's continuation hook cannot trap it), --permission-mode acceptEdits with a configurable allowedTools list, --max-budget-usd, optional --model, own timeout. Its reported total_cost_usd flows into the cycle cost; the harness verifier (receipts + cross-model verdict) checks its work as for the built-in executor. Evidence: claude-code-executor.test (flags, env, cwd, usage/cost, error/invalid/missing binary -> no result; spawn-failure hang found and fixed), cycle.test with the claude-code backend (Claude Code executes, harness verifies and writes implemented, cost 0.3 combined), loop-worker 33/33; real CLI probe with Haiku in a scratch dir returned a valid structured result ($0.005). Missing: Codex backend (codex exec --json) and running in a disposable worktree (needs deps installed there; today it uses loop.worktreePath like the built-in executor).
